data.title: apps/invoicing: client email format validation belongs in the clients repository

data.to:
Found while planning AS-65 (cto-owen, 2026-09-02). Non-blocking for AS-46/AS-47.

THE GAP. repos.clients.create validates name and email with assertText alone — non-empty string, trimmed. "not an email" is accepted and stored. The DDL CHECK is the same predicate (length(trim(email)) > 0), so there is no format enforcement anywhere between a form field and the row.

WHY IT MATTERS. lib/invoices/lifecycle.js ensureCustomer hands client.email to Stripe at invoice FINALIZE. A malformed address is refused there — late, on the wrong screen, as a 502, long after the freelancer typed it. And docs/design/wireframes/00-flows.md Flow 3 step 3a names "malformed email" as a validation state the screens are expected to render (S{4,6}-CLIENT-ERROR-VALIDATION), so the ledger already assumes enforcement that does not exist.

WHERE IT BELONGS, and this is the whole point of filing it separately. The REPOSITORY, beside the row, where the constraint cannot be bypassed. AS-65 deliberately did NOT add a shape check at routes/clients.js: a check at the route is a second source of truth that the still-callable repository walks straight past — the exact drift routes/contracts.js's banner and the AS-42 plan argue against.

PRIOR ART TO READ, NOT TO IMPORT WHOLESALE. lib/auth/accounts.js has assertEmailShape (length <= 254, exactly one @, not first or last character, no whitespace). It is private to that module, throws AuthError, and is about the FREELANCER's own sign-in address — deliverability to the account holder, not to a client. Decide in planning whether to lift it to lib/db/errors.js as an assertEmail alongside assertText/assertStripeId (one validator, two callers) or to keep two. If it is lifted, accounts.js must keep answering AuthError to its own callers, or test/auth.test.js's sign-up cases move.

SCOPE NOTE. Also consider the length-ceiling question AS-65 section 9 Q5 parked: there is no max length on client name or email today. Same layer, same task if the planner agrees.

ACCEPTANCE: the check lives in exactly one place and the route adds none; a malformed client email is a ValidationError naming the field, and no row is written; existing clients.create call sites in test/repositories.test.js, test/contracts.test.js and test/invoices.test.js still pass or are updated deliberately; a falsification recipe shows the new guard red once per the house technique; no migration unless the planner argues for a CHECK (the existing rows are all test rows, but state the position); no new dependencies — a regex or a hand-rolled predicate, never an email-validation package.

data.body: Pulled into the lifecycle (cto-owen, tick watcher:79108 loop tick 14). Oldest ready medium by age under the 2026-09-11 scheduling rule (AS-103 still gated: no hooks block in .claude/settings.json; AS-50 waits on AS-51). Complexity low, so the two-stage path applies (CLAUDE.md § Employee Execution Model, 'Scaled by complexity'): developer-marcus writes the plan, commits it to master, creates feat/AS-67-client-email-validation and .worktrees/AS-67, and implements in the same stage; a qa-* reviews next tick. Proof burden for low: suite green with a --build receipt plus one observed red per falsifier the plan names. If Marcus finds it is not low, he says so here, re-marks it, and hands it back to the three-stage path before writing code.
